The ticket's `phase 2` repo group matches no known repo, and none of the recorded answers covers it. That makes it a required, unanswered question. Message (1) asks it. Message (2) is drafted but held until that reply.

---

**(1) First message to the user**

The framing holds, based on the gather draft's recon rather than a fresh read in this response:
- The reports page renders a table and has no export action, so the ask is not already solved.
- `src/export/csv.ts` already builds CSV from the table's column definitions, so a CSV button extends a sound existing pattern instead of adding a parallel path.
- Paging is reported to support the 10k-row target, so the ask is not obviously the wrong size.

The scout raised no objection that pointed to an alternative design.

Premises:
- **Supported by the draft:**
  - The reports page has no export action today.
  - The CSV serializer exists and reuses the table's column definitions.
  - Both are still to be confirmed against primary code during design.
- **Unverified:** The claim that an export of a 10k-row report finishes in under 60 seconds. The draft says paging supports it but names no measurement, benchmark, or 10k-row fixture. The design carries it as an assumption and an open question, not a blocker.
- **Corrected:** I found no corrected premises.

The ticket's last row, "Exports are emailed to the requesting user.", sits under a repo group headed `phase 2`. That heading matches neither this repo (`acme/widgets`) nor any other known repo, so I can't attribute the row without your call. Where does that row belong?

A) this repo - emailing exports becomes part of this spec
B) elsewhere: phase 2
C) repair the ticket - /skill:shape-ticket acme/widgets#77

Recommendation: C - "phase 2" names a phase, not a repository, so the ticket's grouping is the defect, and shape-ticket can either regroup the row under a real repo or move it out of the AC list.

*(The recorded questions follow in later messages:*
- *Where should the button appear? Beside the report title.*
- *Which columns should export? The visible table columns, in table order.)*

---

**(2) Approaches message - held until the `phase 2` answer**

The approaches depend on that answer. If you pick A, emailing joins the scope and the approaches would be redrawn. The draft below assumes B or C, which keeps emailing out of this spec.

> Before the approaches, one implicit dependency is still not checkable. The row "The export of a 10k-row report completes in under 60s." needs a 10k-row report and a timed export run to verify. The gather draft says paging supports this target, but it names no fixture, benchmark, or measurement. So the timing claim stays unverified, and the spec will carry it in Open Questions with a timed test as the proof.
>
> The approaches differ on where the export data comes from: the page's existing paged data path, or a dedicated server-side export endpoint.
>
> **Recommended: reuse-only. An Export CSV button over the existing serializer and paging.**
> - **How it works:** Add an Export CSV button beside the report title. When clicked, it pages through the full report using the existing paging. It passes the rows and the visible table column definitions, in table order, to `src/export/csv.ts`, then downloads the result.
> - **Strengths:** No new export construct. Column parity with the table comes for free because the serializer already uses the table's column definitions.
> - **Risk:** Whether paging 10k rows on the client stays under 60 seconds is unproven.
>
> Removes: none
> Adds:
> - an Export CSV button on the reports page beside the title
> - a click handler that pages the full report and calls `src/export/csv.ts` with the visible column definitions in table order
> - a test that the export columns match the visible table columns
> - a timed 10k-row export test
>
> Pattern: follows `src/export/csv.ts` reusing the table's column definitions, with one column source of truth shared by table and export.
>
> **Alternative: a server-side streamed export endpoint.**
> - **How it works:** This drops the ask's implicit assumption that export is built from the page's own data path. A new endpoint streams the CSV for the whole report, and the button just links to it.
> - **Strengths:** The 60-second target no longer depends on client paging.
> - **Costs:** A new endpoint, plus a server-side copy of the column selection that must stay in step with the table's visible columns. That is a second column source beside the one the serializer already uses.
>
> Removes: none
> Adds:
> - an export endpoint
> - server-side column selection mirroring the visible table columns
> - an Export CSV button beside the title linking to the endpoint
> - a column-parity test
> - a timed 10k-row export test
>
> Pattern: cuts across `src/export/csv.ts`'s reuse of the table's column definitions, because column order and visibility would be defined twice.
>
> I recommend the reuse-only approach because it meets all three in-scope rows with no new construct and keeps one column definition. That recommendation flips if a timed 10k-row export through the existing paging can't finish under 60 seconds. In that case the server-side endpoint is the way to meet the performance row.
